summary: Governing Council decided to 'raise the three key ECB interest rates by 25 basis points': deposit facility 2.50%, main refinancing operations 2.65%, marginal lending facility 2.90%, with effect from 16 September 2026. bank_rate and previous_bank_rate show the deposit facility rate; the previous 2.25% (in effect from 17 June 2026) is taken from the ECB key interest rates table (https://www.ecb.europa.eu/stats/policy_and_exchange_rates/key_ecb_interest_rates/html/index.en.html), not from the release. Release: the conflict in the Middle East 'continues to generate inflation pressures', and 'inflation is set to remain well above target for an extended period'. September 2026 ECB staff projections: headline inflation 3.0% (2026), 2.5% (2027), 2.1% (2028); inflation excluding energy and food 2.5%, 2.6%, 2.3%; GDP growth 0.9%, 1.4%, 1.5%. 2026 inflation unchanged from June; 2027 and 2028 revised up. The ECB's 10 September 2026 monetary policy decision press release does not publish a vote, so vote and dissent are null. It gives staff projections ("The baseline of the new ECB staff projections sees headline inflation averaging 3.0% in 2026, 2.5% in 2027 and 2.1% in 2028.") but no current inflation figure, so inflation is null.
why_it_matters: The release says the decision 'underscores the Governing Council’s commitment to setting monetary policy to ensure that inflation stabilises at its 2% target in the medium term'. It sees 'risks to the upside for inflation and to the downside for economic growth'. The Governing Council will follow a 'data-dependent and meeting-by-meeting' approach and is 'not pre-committing to a particular rate path'.
